1925, November
FR. SOLANUS, NOTEBOOK NO. 1.
Page 28 Cont.
2/12/25 Terribly Paralyzed. - Will 3rd Enrollment Help ?!!! Veronie Rose 18 of 2060 Boston Boulvd is Enrolled To-night for 3rd time at 10 p.m. - her father having phoned of a seeming relaps, with three terrible convulsions. She has been paralized now about two years and at times has seemed to have sleeping sickness also. A number of times she has been given up as medically hopeless. On the Feast of St. Terese Oct. Ist ( '25) her father consented to build a pro- posed chapel in honor of the same Little Flower - To the memory of his said Daughter Veronica. Fiat Dei Voluntas! .
Sept. 29th '26 .... Sad experiences since last noted - convulsions about Christmas and again after Holy Week with consequent discour- agement and gradual weakening of physical faculties; blind now since about New Years. At 11.30 p.m. this note is being made. Hav- ing been in convulsions every ten minutes this evening from 6. p.m. the doctor came 2nd time - hypodermics and cloriforme failing to af- fect her. She was anointed at 10.30 p.m. They are making Novena to St. Terese. To-morrow is her anniversary. Will she drop a petal on the Family R ..
Sept. 30 A.M. "No Improvement" phoned - Convulsions continue almost uninterruptedly - Except for about two hours after reception of Ex- treme Unction ..... Once during night Nurse anounced: "She is dying now, if she is not dead." P.M. No improvement, convulsions still on!
Oct. Ist Feast of St. Terese. Phone call 7.15 a.m. "Veronica very bad." "Pray for her at this Mass specially." She becomes quiet dur- ing Mass - convulsions having ceased at 2 a.m. At 10.30 a.m. re- ceives Holy Viaticum seemingly semi conscious, swallowing small part- ical - Fever still up. 103 & 104 and over. Just about 12 o'clock she smiles as though victory were in sight and slumbers peacefully after 36 hours fearful exertion and about 200 convulsions. "Has St. Terese appeared to her?" her Mother, Mrs. Rose (a convert) muses. Phone at 4. p.m. "Veronica awakes for few minutes, speaks smiles,
kisses her father and slumbers again, smiling -
V. Rose Case Continued. October 2nd awakes cheerful and smiling remembers some of the experiences during the convulsions or between them.
Octave of Feast. This evening - Friday, as a rule her hardest day -- reported not well at all first time in over a week that improvement seemed only transitory, convulsions starting again though not so severe.
